page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AMD EPYC 7571 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 384 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the system operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests scoring in the bottom 10%. However, the 96-vCPU allocation elevates multi-core performance to average levels, as demonstrated by multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU scores. Memory performance is a highlight, with small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth ranking in the top 25%, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths remain average. Cryptographic execution is also strong, with the Passmark CPU encryption test placing in the top 25%, aided by hardware-accelerated SHA_NI and AES instruction sets.

The m5ad.24xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency by pairing AMD EPYC processors with high-capacity local NVMe SSD storage, reducing the need for external block storage attachments for high-throughput workloads. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and substantial local storage, this instance is suited for workloads such as database hosting, static web serving, multi-threaded data processing, and general-purpose applications that require high-speed local scratch space but do not demand high single-threaded CPU performance.
description: The Amazon Web Services m5ad.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 384 GB of DDR4 memory and 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, alongside a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. While single-core benchmarks for this instance fall in the bottom 10%, its multi-core capabilities and database operations perform at an average tier. Notably, cached small-block memory bandwidth and cryptographic encryption tests rank in the top 25%. Lacking a GPU, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for resource-dense applications requiring high-capacity local storage. It is best suited for database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
